questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: New, interesting region - I could get knowledge about a new area that was relevant for my studies

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very worth it. I gained new academic knowledge and got new academic competences and explored a new area ect.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The institution was very helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The institution picked us up in a van.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Shared or private room. I had shared room. A shared kitchen in two departments of each floor, a shared a toilet in the dorm (4 persons sharing, we were 3 though). TV-rooms, study-rooms. Elevator and stairways. Linnen.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A cantine - a kitchen - automats with food

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There can be some noise sometimes since people stay up late there - also, there are no kitchen utensils in the kitchen, I bought mine myself. Guests can't visit after 22, and not before what I believe was 10 in the morning.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked that it was easy to be with your friends.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took much time, but they were very helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not remember steps into details, anyhow, there was a lot of work, but it was made step-by-step and manageable, therefore it was not overwhelming.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could also ask the international staff and our professors, which was nice. Furthermore, meetings were arranged.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I changed one of the classes. I liked my classes, though, especially two of them that were about politics.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you follow the steps and the deadlines, everything should be fine, and as long as you do that, there is no need to to stress.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They were having the American-style-university model, which means it was different from ours. In some ways I liked it, and some ways I liked our model in Denmark better. We had 3 midtterm exams, which means all of the stress and expectations were not linked to only one exam, so in that way exams were more relaxed. However, it also meant that much were about the specific exams and testing all the time, and in that way I like our better, that we, to a bigger extend, focus on learning. Also, one would realize that in Denmark, when studying at a university, you are the one responsible for your learning, you decide yourself whether or not you want to attend the classes. Here, a certain percentage of classes were mandatory.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They start at university earlier, which means that there was some difference, you did gain knowledge, though, but if you want to have academic levels comparative to ours, you probably need to take some of the senior-bachelor courses or master courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As mentioned earlier, they use another system, the American one, so at some aspects you can't really compare them.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Central Asia in Global Politics, Foreign Politics of Kazakhstan, History of Kazakhstan

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Central Asia in Global Politics (master course, but both home and host University allowed us to take it)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Maybe that the sports were actually quite expensive. If you wanted to attend sport outside the uni. Because the ones at uni were for free, where for example they had a running club, for free, and a free gym

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I used taxies pretty much as they were easy and cheap, however, you could drive in busses and metroes (metroes I also did pretty much) for almost no money.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My running club at the university was nice.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Several arrangement. Parties and other. Language clubs ect.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Running club if you like to run

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips!! Explore the culture, but also, the besides learning about culture and academics, the nature is impressing. Trips there are cheap, if you buy them at local places (of course choose the safe-ones that other people go on, that are actual companies)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Of course, another culture, but people were very friendly. Also, they seem quite open, so you open up yourself more

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open. People do not really judge.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe that in Denmark we have specific ways of doing things, so maybe that. However, I pretty fast got some good friends, so I didn't think about it to much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That they were friendly and welcoming

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Explore the area and have fun. And regarding more "serious": be aware that the air pollution is pretty bad, be aware that there is meat in most meals

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: That you need to attend many of the classes - also, that staying on campus is a good way to socialize.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I would actually say the people I met there. However, also some competences and academic confidence I due to mandatory presentations, especially due to a presentation in our master class.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That I had to addapt to the food and air, the first day, I got food posioned. After that it was fine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: All the paper work for exchange were worth the experience!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
